title: Federal money the City passes on: its own audit against its reports to Washington
question: The City’s audited accounts say how much federal money it handed to subrecipients. How much of that did it report to the federal subaward register, programme by programme?
finding: The City’s own audited schedules say it provided $775.0 million of federal money to subrecipients in fiscal 2021 to 2025 ($158.5 million in 2021; $153.5 million in 2022; $160.2 million in 2023; $135.4 million in 2024; $167.4 million in 2025). The subawards it reported to the federal register with dates in the same five years come to $199.2 million: 26%. For the Continuum of Care homeless-housing programme the schedules show $177.0 million provided to subrecipients and the register shows $1.5 million ($7.5 million counting every City report on file, 2015 to 2021). 13 programmes with $5 million or more provided show no report at all, led by 97.067 Homeland Security Grant Program ($60.9 million); 93.558 Temporary Assistance for Needy Families ($40.4 million); 93.959 Block Grants for Prevention and Treatment of Substance ($36.1 million); 93.658 Foster Care Title IV-E ($30.0 million). Recipients’ own audits record $638.8 million received through the City in the same years, far more than the register. In 6 programmes the recipients’ auditors record more than the City says it provided to subrecipients at all: 93.558 Temporary Assistance for Needy Families ($83.1 million in recipients’ audits, $40.4 million in the City’s); 93.778 Medical Assistance Program ($57.6 million in recipients’ audits, $17.4 million in the City’s); 97.036 Disaster Grants - Public Assistance ($38.3 million in recipients’ audits, $2.1 million in the City’s), which suggests the City treats as contractors bodies whose auditors treat the money as a federal award.
how: City side: the column “Amount Provided to Subrecipients” in the schedule of expenditures of federal awards in each of the City’s five single audit reports, fiscal 2021 to 2025, summed by federal assistance listing number; each year’s parsed sum is checked against the printed grand total. Register side: subawards under City prime awards on USAspending with action dates 1 July 2020 to 30 June 2025, exact duplicate rows removed. Third column: award lines in the clearinghouse audits of City-paid organizations that name the City as the pass-through body, audit years 2021 to 2025.
limits: Nothing here says money went astray: the City’s auditors tested these programmes and the recipients’ audits show the money arriving. The gap is in what the public register shows, so no outsider can list who received the City’s federal homeless-housing or welfare money from it. Any of these would produce the same picture: a report filed late or against a different prime award number; a subaward dated before July 2020 and spent in these years; programmes that reach the City through the State, where the State may be the body that reports; the register gives an amount awarded on a date, the schedule an amount spent in a year. What the reporting rule requires for each programme is not in the files on disk; the City’s auditors raised no finding on it in these years. For the fiscal years covered here, the federal audit threshold depends on the start of the entity’s fiscal year. It was $750,000 in federal awards expended across all programs for years starting before October 1, 2024, and $1 million for years starting on or after that date. An entity reaches the threshold at either amount. City payments alone cannot establish how much federal funding the recipient expended.
